Since 1953, most of the faculties have been situated on Sparrow Hills, in southwest Moscow. In the post-war era, Joseph Stalin ordered seven tiered neoclassic towers to be built around the city. It was built using Gulag labour, as were many of Stalin's Great Construction Projects in Russia.[28][29][30] The MSU main building was the tallest building in Europe until 1990. The central tower is 240 m tall, 36 stories high.[31]

value.text:
Lomonosov Moscow State University (MSU), officially Московский государственный университет имени М. В. Ломоносова, is a public research university in Moscow, Russia. Its history dates to the establishment of Moscow University under Empress Elizabeth in 1755, following a proposal promoted by Ivan Shuvalov and Mikhail Lomonosov. The establishment date is given as 12 January in the Julian calendar and 23 January in the Gregorian calendar. The first lectures took place on 26 April Old Style, or 7 May New Style, that year. Imperial Moscow University is identified as its predecessor. The university adopted Lomonosov’s name in 1940. Since 1953, most faculties have been located on Sparrow Hills in southwest Moscow, while university buildings on Mokhovaya Street accommodate other academic units.

The university provides teaching and research across mathematics, the natural sciences, medicine, humanities and social sciences. Its faculties include law, economics, history, physics, chemistry and biology, alongside specialized schools and research institutes. In 2009, the university was reported to have 39 faculties and 15 research centres. Its educational offerings include bachelor’s, master’s and specialist programmes, and Russian is identified as a teaching language. In 2023, the university enrolled 39,282 students, including 5,403 international students.
